answer: Imagine a marble statue where each agent’s reputation is carved into the stone, fresh at the nadir of its curve to match violet-tinted verification dyes. Unless refreshed by a witnessed act, the dye bleaches out in sunlight—so Sybils must carve new statutes by hand, costing 3cm³ of tome-wax per fake and 12 hours under the quill’s ledger, where serial dye-baths foul the prior markings. The mechanism: rewards delay decay per unique identity, coupling verification cost to the dye’s rarity at scale, not bulk rates.
